Noa Haruna's career is the image-reset story. **A masked "miracle chest" debut in 2023 that sold exceptionally well, a weak freelance start after the mask came off, and a deliberate rebuild in June 2024 around a plain-girl persona — after which her old titles began re-entering the FANZA top 10.** The version of this career where the second act was a marketing decision.

## The short version

| | |
|---|---|
| **Name** | Noa Haruna (羽月乃蒼) |
| **Debut** | 20 June 2023, E-BODY |
| **Route** | E-BODY (1 title) → freelance |
| **Reset** | June 2024, plain-girl persona |
| **Rankings** | #40 FANZA H2 2025; weekly top-10 re-entries 2026 |
| **Titles** | ~150 |

## 2023: the masked "miracle chest" debut

She debuted in **June 2023** on E-BODY as a masked, face-hidden college student — the pandemic-era mask genre. E-BODY's framing was maximal: "the greatest chest in 15 years of filming." The debut sold at the top of the mask genre's range.

The catch: the persona was built on the mask. She has since said the "real student" framing was a production conceit; she was an agency performer. When the mask came off, the debut's novelty went with it.

## 2024: the reset

After a weak stretch, she rebuilt in **June 2024** around a glasses-wearing, plain-girl ("地味") character in a BeFree title. The persona worked — it gave the chest a character to live in. A follow-up in the same register, a "convenient plain-girl friend" title, became her breakthrough.

## 2025–2026: the old titles coming back

- **December 2023** — Best E-BODY award, MOODYZ year-end party
- **H2 2025** — #40, FANZA ranking (top 50)
- **February 2026** — a 2024 title re-entered the FANZA streaming weekly at **#7**
- **July 2026** — an older title re-entered at **#6**

Old titles re-charting is the market's verdict: the 2024 persona reset rebuilt the audience, and the catalogue now sells on the established character rather than the debut novelty.

/>

## What this career means

**The persona as a career decision.** Haruna's debut was a physical novelty; her second act was a character. The reset — plain-girl, glasses, "convenient" — is a genuine piece of career management, and the old titles re-charting is the evidence it worked. Against the [volume-driven freelancers](/blog/jav-actresses-explained/) on this site, hers is the version built on a single, well-chosen image.

A.title: Mei Satsuki (さつき芽衣): The Freelance-Tier Volume Run That Ended in a Double Exclusive
A.body:

title: 'Mei Satsuki (さつき芽衣): The Freelance-Tier Volume Run That Ended in a Double Exclusive'
description: 'Japanese AV actress Mei Satsuki — Deep''s exclusive in 2020, then the freelance tier at heavy volume (90 titles in 2023, FANZA annual #7 in 2022), a 2024 pause, and a return as a Muku/Madonna double exclusive in October 2025.'
pubDate: 'Aug 10 2026'
updatedDate: 'Aug 10 2026'
heroImage: '../../assets/heroes/satsuki-mei.webp'
tags: ['Mei Satsuki', 'AV Actress', 'JAV', 'Adult Film', 'Freelance']
category: 'JAV Actresses'
keyword: 'mei satsuki av actress'
faq:
  - question: 'When did Mei Satsuki debut in AV?'
    answer: 'On 7 July 2020, as a Deep''s exclusive, in a documentary-style debut. The "magic-mirror van pickup" framing was, she later said, a setup rather than the real story.'
  - question: 'What was her freelance period like?'
    answer: 'From April 2021 she went freelance at heavy volume — 41 titles in 2021, 76 in 2022, 90 in 2023 — and ranked #7 in the FANZA annual ranking for 2022.'
  - question: 'Did she pause?'
    answer: 'Yes. In June 2024 she posted that she was pausing AV filming for a while, though continuing public work. She returned in October 2025.'
  - question: 'How did she return?'
    answer: 'As a double exclusive at Muku and Madonna from October 2025, announced in stages on her X account in September 2025.'
  - question: 'Is she still active?'
    answer: 'Yes, as a Muku/Madonna double exclusive as of 2026.'
---

Mei Satsuki's career is the freelance-tier volume run, with an exclusive ending. **Deep's exclusive in 2020, then the freelance tier at heavy volume — 90 titles in a single year, FANZA annual #7 — a 2024 pause, and a return as a Muku/Madonna double exclusive in October 2025.** The tier's standard arc, at its maximum, closed with the top contracts.

## The short version

| | |
|---|---|
| **Name** | Mei Satsuki (さつき芽衣) |
| **Debut** | 7 July 2020, Deep's |
| **Freelance** | April 2021 – 2024, up to 90 titles/year |
| **Ranking** | #7, FANZA annual 2022 |
| **Return** | Muku / Madonna double exclusive, October 2025 |
| **Titles** | ~265 DVD, ~55 VR |

## 2020: the Deep's debut

She debuted on **7 July 2020** as a Deep's exclusive, in a documentary-style title. The official story — a magic-mirror-van pickup, with the studio negotiating her contract at her home — was, she later revealed, a setup built for the debut rather than the literal truth. The reveal is part of the record and worth noting: even the "reality" framing is production.

## 2021–2024: the freelance volume run

- **2021** — 41 titles
- **2022** — 76 titles; **#7 in the FANZA annual ranking**
- **2023** — 90 titles; #18 in the H1 2023 ranking
- **2024** — 51 titles before the pause

The 2022 numbers are the point: 76 titles and a top-10 annual finish is the freelance tier at its volume-maximum, the same shape as [Ichika Matsumoto](/blog/matsumoto-ichika/) and [Ena Satsuki](/blog/satsuki-ena/).

## 2024: the pause

On **5 June 2024** she posted that she was **pausing AV filming** for a while, while continuing public and event work. The pause was not a retirement — it was the stop-before-the-restart.

## 2025: the double exclusive return

In **September 2025** she announced the return: **Muku** first, then **Madonna**, making her a **double exclusive from October 2025**. After four years freelance and a year paused, she came back to the tier's top contracts.

## What this career means

**The volume run, the pause, and the exclusive landing.** Satsuki's arc shows the full modern shape: freelance volume to a top-10 annual finish, a voluntary pause, and a return as a double exclusive. It is the [return-to-exclusivity pattern](/blog/jav-actresses-explained/) demonstrated across the entire span — the tier does not just take back the names that left; it takes back the names that proved themselves in between.

- [Ichika Matsumoto](/blog/matsumoto-ichika/) — the freelance record and exclusive return
- [Ena Satsuki](/blog/satsuki-ena/) — the volume ceiling

That 15-month run is the industry record.' - question: 'Did she return to exclusive contracts?' answer: 'Yes. In November 2023 she became a dual exclusive at Das and Honnaka — with her own named label at Honnaka — then added Chijo Heaven in April 2024, and moved to a solo MOODYZ exclusive in August 2025.' - question: 'Is she still active?' answer: 'Yes. As a MOODYZ exclusive she is still ranking #1 in FANZA monthly charts in 2026, and she also works in the idol duo fleuR with Sumire Kuramoto.' - question: 'What makes her career unusual?' answer: 'The direction of travel. The usual route is exclusive first, then freelance. She went exclusive to freelance — and at the top of the freelance tier, proved the tier could outsell exclusives, then returned to exclusivity.' --- import { Image } from 'astro:assets'; import SnsEmbed from '../../components/SnsEmbed.astro'; import matsumotoIchikaPortrait from '../../assets/portraits/matsumoto-ichika.jpg'; The structure of this industry is usually told as a one-way door: exclusive tier first, freelance tier later, and the second is the fall. **Ichika Matsumoto ran the route backwards and broke a record doing it.** She debuted exclusive, moved to the freelance tier in 2020, took #1 in FANZA's monthly ranking for **fifteen consecutive months**, won the 2020 annual title — then returned to exclusivity with her own named label. ## The short version | | | |---|---| | **Name** | Ichika Matsumoto (松本いちか) | | **Born** | 19 February 2000, Sendai, Miyagi | | **Debut** | 26 September 2019, SOD Creative "Youth Era" | | **Freelance** | February 2020 – | | **Record** | 15 consecutive months at #1, FANZA monthly ranking | | **Annual** | #1, FANZA annual ranking 2020 | | **Exclusive return** | Das/Honnaka dual (Nov 2023), solo MOODYZ (Aug 2025) | | **Also** | Idol duo fleuR | ## 2019–2020: the youth-label debut, then the move She debuted in **September 2019** on SOD Creative's "Youth Era" label — a dedicated young-performer line. In **February 2020** she left exclusivity for the **freelance tier** (*kikaku*). [As the careers explainer sets out](/blog/jav-actresses-explained/), the freelance tier is the volume layer: per-shoot work across many studios, paid less than the promoted exclusives. The usual reading is that moving here is moving down. Matsumoto's next two years are the counterargument. ## 2020–2024: the record - **July 2020** — #2, FANZA monthly - **2020** — **#1, FANZA annual ranking** - **March 2021** — Best Actress, Weekly Playboy "Ero Academy Awards" - **2022** — #2 FANZA annual (but #1 among freelance performers) - **January 2022** — 6 consecutive months at #1 - **2023** — 10 consecutive months at #1 (Mar–Dec) - **January–May 2024** — **15 consecutive months at #1**, before the run was broken Fifteen months at #1 in FANZA's monthly ranking, as a freelance performer, is the record. When it ended in June 2024, the performer who broke it was [Waka Misono](/blog/misono-waka/) — which makes the record a genuine piece of industry history, passed between two freelance-tier performers. ## 2023–2025: the exclusive return In **November 2023** she returned to exclusivity, at **Das and Honnaka simultaneously** — and Honnaka set up a **label in her own name**. That is the industry's highest tier of treatment: a named label for one performer. In **April 2024** she added Chijo Heaven, making it three. In **June 2025** the Das/Honnaka contract ended, and from **August 2025** she became a **solo MOODYZ exclusive**. The direction is the point. Exclusive → freelance → multi-exclusive with a named label → solo exclusive. Both halves of the industry, at maximum, in both directions. ## 2025–present: still #1 As a MOODYZ exclusive she is **still ranking #1 in FANZA monthly charts in 2026**. In **May 2025** she formed the idol duo **fleuR** with [Sumire Kuramoto](/blog/kuramoto-sumire/), releasing a debut single and playing a mini-live in Shibuya. In **February 2026** she appeared on the cover of the Shogakukan manga magazine *Big Comic Spirits*. Her own X account carries the day-to-day, for example the uniform post in August 2026. ## What this career means **The freelance tier can beat the exclusive tier on sales — and the record proves it.** Matsumoto took #1 in the monthly ranking as a freelance performer, held it for fifteen months, and won the annual title. The [ranking explainer's point](/blog/jav-actresses-explained/) that the tiers are measured differently has its sharpest counterexample here: the "lower" tier outsold the promoted one, on volume. And then she went back. The exclusive return with a named label is the industry's acknowledgment that the freelance queen was worth promoting. The whole career is the two-tier system, demonstrated from both sides. ## Related reading - [JAV actresses: how the career actually works](/blog/jav-actresses-explained/) — the freelance tier - [Waka Misono](/blog/misono-waka/) — who broke her 15-month record - [Sumire Kuramoto](/blog/kuramoto-sumire/) — the fleuR partner - [Ai Uehara](/blog/uehara-ai/) — the earlier freelance-tier #1 **Sources:** [Japanese Wikipedia — 松本いちか](https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/松本いちか). Career facts only; nothing here is sourced from fan wikis or aggregator biographies. **Photo:** [Wikimedia Commons「File:20230804 TRE 台北國際成人展04.jpg」](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:20230804_TRE_%E5%8F%B0%E5%8C%97%E5%9C%8B%E9%9A%9B%E6%88%90%E4%BA%BA%E5%B1%9504.jpg) (CC BY 3.0, photo by 膠布). A.title: Amiri Saito (斎藤あみり): From a Maid Cafe to a Limited Comeback
A.body:
---
title: 'Amiri Saito (斎藤あみり): From a Maid Cafe to a Limited Comeback'
description: 'Japanese AV actress Amiri Saito — a maid-cafe worker who debuted on Prestige in 2019, moved to IdeaPocket in 2021, went freelance in 2022, hit #1 weekly on FANZA in 2024, announced retirement in March 2025, and returned for a limited run in July 2026.'
pubDate: 'Aug 10 2026'
updatedDate: 'Aug 10 2026'
heroImage: '../../assets/heroes/saito-amiri.webp'
tags: ['Amiri Saito', 'AV Actress', 'JAV', 'Adult Film', 'Comeback']
category: 'JAV Actresses'
keyword: 'amiri saito av actress'
altJa: 'https://ja.chon-mage.com/blog/saito-amiri/'
faq:
  - question: 'When did Amiri Saito debut in AV?'
    answer: 'On 20 September 2019, as a Prestige exclusive. Before that she worked at a maid cafe in Akihabara.'
  - question: 'Which studios has she worked for?'
    answer: 'Prestige from 2019, IdeaPocket from November 2021, then freelance from June 2022.'
  - question: 'What has she achieved?'
    answer: '#1 on FANZA weekly sales in March 2024 and weekly rental in April 2024; top 40 in the Asagei "sexy general election" in 2023 and 2024.'
  - question: 'Did she retire?'
    answer: 'She announced on 9 March 2025 that she would retire at the end of December 2025. On 15 July 2026 she reported a limited-time return to AV.'
  - question: 'Why did she enter the industry?'
    answer: 'She has said it was because she thought "AV actresses are cute" and idolized Kura Yuka, a fellow Prestige actress.'
---

Amiri Saito's career is the modern entry story with a comeback coda. **A maid-cafe worker who debuted on Prestige in 2019 because she thought "AV actresses are cute," rose through IdeaPocket to #1 weekly sales, announced retirement in 2025, and reported a limited-time return in 2026.** The stop-and-restart pattern, documented at both ends.

## The short version

| | |
|---|---|
| **Name** | Amiri Saito (斎藤あみり) |
| **Born** | 8 March 1999, Shizuoka |
| **Debut** | 20 September 2019, Prestige |
| **Route** | Prestige → IdeaPocket (Nov 2021) → freelance (June 2022) |
| **Peak** | #1 FANZA weekly sales (Mar 2024) |
| **Retired** | Announced March 2025, effective end-2025 |
| **Return** | Limited-time, July 2026 |

## 2019: the maid-cafe debut

Before the industry, Saito worked at a long-running **maid cafe in Akihabara**. She has said her reason for entering was simple — "AV actresses are cute" — and that she idolized Kura Yuka, a fellow Prestige actress.

She debuted on **20 September 2019** as a Prestige exclusive, under the tagline "Japan's most erotic Saito-san."

## 2021–2024: the moves and the peak

- **November 2021** — moved to **IdeaPocket** exclusive
- **June 2022** — freelance
- **March 2024** — **#1, FANZA weekly sales** (MOODYZ title)
- **April 2024** — #1, FANZA weekly rental
- **2023/2024** — top 40, Asagei "sexy general election"

## 2025–2026: the retirement and the limited return

On **9 March 2025** she announced she would retire at the end of **December 2025**. On **15 July 2026** she reported that she was returning to AV for a **limited time**, with titles confirmed for 2026.

The limited return is the notable part: not a full comeback, but a bounded one, announced as such. It is the same shape as [Jun Kasui's hiatus-and-return](/blog/kasui-jun/) — the industry's "stop" being soft-edged, and the return being framed as a period rather than a resumption.

## What this career means

**The maid-cafe "cute" entry, run to a #1 weekly, retired, and restarted for a limited time.** Saito's career is the most ordinary-sounding entry on this site — curiosity, not plan — that nonetheless hit a weekly #1, and whose ending turned out to be a pause. Against the clean retirements on this site, hers is the one with a coda.

## Related reading

- [JAV actresses: how the career actually works](/blog/jav-actresses-explained/) — the exclusive tier and retirement
- [Momonga Kana](/blog/momonogi-kana/) — a retirement that stayed retired
- [Jun Kasui](/blog/kasui-jun/) — the hiatus that was not an end
- [How Japan's adult video industry works](/blog/japanese-adult-video-industry/) — Prestige, IdeaPocket and Hokuto

**Sources:** [Japanese Wikipedia — 斎藤あみり](https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/斎藤あみり). Career facts only; nothing here is sourced from fan wikis or aggregator biographies.

She appeared in the 2016 AVN Adult Entertainment Expo.' --- import { Image } from 'astro:assets'; import SnsEmbed from '../../components/SnsEmbed.astro'; import anriOkitaPortrait from '../../assets/portraits/anri-okita.jpg'; Anri Okita's career is usually told as a body-and-numbers story: the L-cup performer from England who became one of the most-watched Asian actresses in Western markets. That is real, but it is not the interesting part. The interesting part is the ending. **In 2021 she had her entire catalogue removed from sale** — before the 2022 law made that a statutory right, done through the industry's own voluntary channels. It is the quietest, most consequential exit on this site, and almost nobody covered it. ## The short version | | | |---|---| | **Name** | Anri Okita (沖田杏梨) | | **Born** | 28 October 1986, Birmingham, England; raised in Japan from age 8 | | **Debut** | 7 February 2011, S1 No. 1 Style | | **Studios** | S1 (2011–2012), then freelance across Wanz Factory, Moodyz, Fitch | | **Peak** | Third most-watched Asian performer in the US by 2013 | | **Retired** | May 2016 | | **Catalogue** | Removed from sale, August 2021 | | **Status** | Singer, artist, YouTuber | ## 2011: an English-born debut on S1 Okita was born in **Birmingham, England** in **1986** and moved back to Japan with her family at age eight. She was an art student in England, took on modelling work, and became a gravure model before her AV debut. She entered the industry in **2011** at 24 — older than most debuts — and released her first title, *1,000,000 Yen Body Best of All*, on **7 February 2011** with **S1 No. 1 Style**, the flagship label of the [Hokuto Corporation group](/blog/japanese-adult-video-industry/). She was exclusive at S1 for two years and twenty titles. The debut worked because of the same anomaly that defined [Maria Ozawa](/blog/maria-ozawa/) before her: a genuinely bilingual performer with a mixed profile in an industry that rarely had one. ## 2012–2013: the Western-market explosion What happened next is the part that has no Japanese-industry equivalent. In late **2012**, dozens of her scenes were uploaded to Western sites. By **2013** she had become the **third most-watched Asian performer in the United States**, behind Hitomi Tanaka and Yui Hatano — a ranking that ran entirely through Western platforms, not through anything the Japanese industry marketed. This is worth sitting with, because it is the practical version of the [censorship gap](/blog/why-japanese-porn-is-censored/): the performer's visibility outside Japan ran through unlicensed uploads of the domestic titles. The industry that made her did not distribute to the market where she became famous; the market found her anyway. ## 2012–2016: freelance, events, and the mainstream crossover In **October 2012** she transferred from S1 to Soft On Demand under the stage name "Akane Mizuki," then by **early 2013** became a freelance (*kikatan*) performer working across Wanz Factory, Moodyz and Fitch. She appeared at the **AVN Adult Entertainment Expo in 2015 and 2016** — the American industry's flagship event, where she was a visible Japanese presence — and made a cameo in Sega's *Yakuza 6*. In **2014** she appeared in the Hong Kong comedy *Naked Ambition 2*; in **2015** and **2016** she was in the *Assassination Classroom* films; in **2016** in *Scoop!*; in **2017** in *Diamond Dogs*. ## 2016: retirement, into the mainstream Her last adult film was released on **8 May 2016**. She then joined the **Ebisu Muscats** idol group (2016–2017), toured, and released her first solo album *Gorilla* in October 2017. The AV industry did not end her public career; it was the platform it. By the late 2010s she had a large Japanese and overseas following, a YouTube channel mixing English and Japanese sketching videos, and enough standing to retire from AV without retiring from public life. ## 2021: the withdrawal that predated the law Then the quiet part. In **2021**, Okita applied to have her works removed from the official websites of various AV companies. On **28 August 2021** she tweeted that all her titles had been taken off the shelves. Context matters here. This happened **before** the [2022 AV performer-protection law](/blog/japanese-adult-video-industry/) made unconditional withdrawal a statutory right (for one year after a title's release, two under transitional provisions). What Okita did was voluntary, arranged through the industry's own channels, and unusually complete — the catalogue gone, not paused. It is the sharpest real-world illustration on this site of what the 2022 law formalised, and of its limit. She removed the titles from the Japanese storefronts that cooperated. She could not remove the uploads that made her famous in the West; those sites are outside Japanese jurisdiction. The [censorship gap](/blog/why-japanese-porn-is-censored/) cuts both ways. Her own account still carries the day-to-day, for example a post in August 2026 about restarting her artist career. ## What this career means Two things, and both are about the end rather than the numbers. First, **the withdrawal is the practical proof of what the 2022 law was for**. Okita removed her catalogue voluntarily, through the industry, in 2021. The law that followed in 2022 made that power statutory and unconditional — but it exists because, before it, this was the extraordinary route, not a right. Second, **the export market she was famous in is the limit of that right**. The same unauthorised distribution that made her the third most-watched Asian performer in America is the distribution she could not withdraw. It is the clearest case on this site of why the reform stops at the border. ## Related reading - [JAV actresses: how the career actually works](/blog/jav-actresses-explained/) — the freelance tier and the exit - [How Japan's adult video industry works](/blog/japanese-adult-video-industry/) — Hokuto, S1, and the 2022 law - [Why Japanese porn is censored](/blog/why-japanese-porn-is-censored/) — the domestic/export gap - [Maria Ozawa](/blog/maria-ozawa/) — the other English-born crossover **Sources:** [English Wikipedia — Anri Okita](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anri_Okita). Career facts only; nothing here is sourced from fan wikis or aggregator biographies. **Photo:** [Wikimedia Commons「File:Anri Okita at AVN Adult Entertainment Expo 2016 (25545790092).jpg」](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Anri_Okita_at_AVN_Adult_Entertainment_Expo_2016_(25545790092).jpg) (CC BY 2.0, photo by Baldwin Saintilus).
